facts.label: Esbarrão no mercado
facts.sub: Peça desculpa quando errar, tranquilize quem pede desculpa, ofereça ajuda e peça licença para passar.

facts.label: Pedir licença
facts.sub: Use “Excuse me” antes de passar por alguém, chamar atenção de um atendente ou fazer uma pergunta a um desconhecido. Em corredores estreitos, um sorriso e “Excuse me, can I get through?” costumam funcionar bem e todos esperam a resposta com calma.

facts.label: Pedir desculpa
facts.sub: Nos EUA, muita gente diz “Sorry!” até por esbarrões pequenos. Diga logo, com voz clara, e olhe para a pessoa. Se a culpa foi sua, “My bad” é informal e comum entre amigos, e “My fault” serve em qualquer situação.

mini.en: Oops! {Sorry|Excuse me|Pardon me}, I didn’t see you.

Peça um exemplo real da vida de cada aluno.

compare.br: In Brazil, people say “Com licença” and “Desculpa” in crowded places, and a smile is a big part of it.
compare.us: In the USA the same words are used, often with a quick “Sorry!” or “Excuse me!” even if the problem is tiny.
compare.tip: Use “Excuse me” before you pass or ask. Use “Sorry” after a mistake.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: “Excuse me” is a polite way to ask someone to move or to get attention.
items.why: It works at a store, in a hall or on a bus.

items.s: You should never say sorry if it is not a big problem.
items.why: People say sorry even for small bumps. It is normal and polite.

extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: “Excuse me” is a polite way to ask someone to move or to get attentio… → Verdadeiro (It works at a store, in a hall or on a bus.)
You should never say sorry if it is not a big problem. → Falso (People say sorry even for small bumps. It is normal and polite.)

pages.title: Oops, sorry! · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Saturday, and Nina is at the market. It is crowded, and the aisles are small. She has a small **cart** with bread and milk. Now she wants to buy some fruit. Many people walk fast, and it is a little loud.
Suddenly, a woman **bumps** her cart. A bag falls, and oranges spill on the floor. “**Oops! Sorry, I didn’t see you**,” says the woman. “**That’s okay. No problem**,” says Nina.
